title: Aquinas infers latria for Christ’s Cross (and even for other cross-effigies by representation) from ‘O cross, hail, only hope’
source_text: XXIII. Hanc vero precationem ad crucem, ut a Christo distinguitur, dirigi, sicut ex ipsius hymni verbis manifestum est, agnovit Thomas Aquinas Scholae Romanae princeps. Inde enim colligit crucem esse cultu Latriae adorandam, hoc utens argumento, Illi exhibemus latriae cultum in quo ponimus spem salutis. Sed in cruce Christi ponimus spem salutis: cantat enim Ecclesia, O crux ave spes unica, Hoc Passionis tempore, Auge piis justitiam, Reisque dona veniam. Ergo Crux Christi est adoranda adoratione latriae. Articuli vero conclusio his verbis concepta est, Crux Christi in qua Christus crucifixus est, tum propter repraesentationem, tum etiam propter membrorum Christi contactum, latria adoranda est: crucis vero effigies in alia quavis materia, priori tantum ratione latria adoranda est. In Summa parte tertia quaestione 25. Articulo quarto.
pass_a_gloss: But that this prayer is directed to the cross as it is distinguished from Christ, as is manifest from the hymn’s own words, Thomas Aquinas, prince of the Roman School, acknowledged. For thence he gathers that the cross is to be adored with the cult of Latria, using this argument: We exhibit to that one the cult of latria in which we place the hope of salvation. But in the cross of Christ we place the hope of salvation: for the Church sings, O cross, hail, only hope… Therefore the Cross of Christ is to be adored with the adoration of latria. And the conclusion of the article is conceived in these words: The Cross of Christ on which Christ was crucified, both because of representation and also because of contact with Christ’s members, is to be adored with latria: but an effigy of the cross in any other material is to be adored with latria only by the former reason. In the Summa, third part, question 25, article four.
pass_b_english: Aquinas reads the hymn as prayer to the cross-as-distinct and concludes the true Cross is owed latria (representation plus contact), and other cross-images latria by representation alone (ST III q.25 a.4).

lemmas.gloss: because of contact with Christ’s members

choices.why: School head draws latria for the cross from official hymn-hope.
rejected: hope only in Christ, never in the cross
